title: Eudiometry Analysis of Atmospheric Oxygen Percentage
author: Josep Grau
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba7aihie

steps.title: Prepare polysulfide solution (500 ml)
steps.instruction: Mix 391.5 g distilled water, 74.5 g elemental sulfur (S), and 34 g calcium oxide (CaO) to obtain 500 ml of polysulfide solution; for larger volumes keep the weight percentages at 78.3 % water, 14.9 % S, and 6.8 % CaO.

steps.title: Boil solution for one hour
steps.instruction: Bring the mixture to a boil and maintain boiling for 1 hour, replenishing water as needed to keep the total volume at 500 ml; the finished solution should appear deep orange, nearly red.

steps.title: Collect 100 ml atmospheric air
steps.instruction: Using a long volumetric tube (A) closed at one end and with a total volume >100 ml, submerge the tube open side down in a water bath and allow air to escape until exactly 100 ml of air remains inside the tube.

steps.title: Combine air with polysulfide solution
steps.instruction: Introduce at least 100 ml of the polysulfide solution into a volumetric flask (B) – excess is recommended – using a flask with a sealable narrow opening slightly larger than tube A; quickly place flask B upside‑down in the water bath, then insert tube A upside‑down and bubble its 100 ml of air into flask B containing the polysulfide solution.

steps.title: Vigorously shake to react
steps.instruction: Seal flask B and shake it vigorously for up to 5 minutes to create many air bubbles, ensuring rapid reaction of oxygen with the polysulfide at the bubble‑liquid interface; longer shaking may be needed if water has diffused into the flask or if polysulfide concentration is low.

steps.title: Measure remaining air volume
steps.instruction: Submerge vessels A and B in the water bath, make sure tube A is completely filled with water, then carefully release the air from flask B, bubbling it into tube A (a funnel can assist); record the final volume of air in tube A, which should be less than the initial 100 ml (expected ≈79 ml). Calculate atmospheric oxygen as 100 ml − 79 ml = 21 % v/v.
